decisions.quote: The coefficient for “Male & had 1st birth” suggests that becoming a parent leads men to more strongly support a traditional division of labor in relation to the care of children (Coefficient = 0.13, SE = 0.05, p = 0.014). The reproduction sample included 14,553 individuals and 29,228 observations. The reproduction results are in line with the findings in the original paper (Coefficient = 0.11, p < 0.05, and a sample of 14,439 individuals and 28,857 observations). Consequently, this reproduction was successful according to the SCORE criteria.
decisions.reason: Under the codebook rules for outcome_computation, only whether re-running the analysis recovered the original reported numbers matters. Although the reproduction succeeded on inferential SCORE criteria, it did not recover the original numbers beyond rounding: the reconstructed HILDA analysis yielded a focal coefficient of 0.13 (SE = 0.05, p = 0.014) with 14,553 individuals and 29,228 observations, whereas the original paper reported a coefficient of 0.11 (p < 0.05) with 14,439 individuals and 28,857 observations, following ambiguities in variable construction and wave availability noted under Deviations from the Original Study. Because the analysis ran and produced comparable output but the reported numbers were not obtained (coefficients and sample sizes differed), the correct value is 'computational issues'.
